article.excerpt: Happy Diwali in 14 Indian languages, from தீபாவளி நல்வாழ்த்துகள் to दिवाळीच्या हार्दिक शुभेच्छा, with each word checked in a named dictionary and the day each region greets in 2027.

article.metaDescription: Happy Diwali in different languages: 14 greetings in native script with transliteration, literal meaning and the dictionary page each word was checked against.
article.keywords: happy diwali in different languages, happy diwali in tamil, happy diwali in kannada, happy diwali in marathi, happy diwali in sanskrit, deepavali greetings
keyTakeaways: Most Indian-language Diwali greetings mean "good wishes of Diwali": the festival's name, a word for "of", and a noun built on Sanskrit śubha, "auspicious".
All 14 greetings here were checked word by word on 22 October 2026 against named dictionaries such as the Tamil Lexicon, Kittel and Molesworth; 5 points could not be fully verified and are listed.
The day differs by language: Tamil households greet at dawn on Thursday 28 October 2027, North India on Friday 29 October, and the Gujarati new year greeting comes on Saturday 30 October.
48.3% of pages shared on SubhSandesh are opened on a phone and each is viewed 11.1 times on average (September 2026), so a misspelt greeting is read again and again.
2 of the 5 top-ranking pages in India on 22 October 2026 carried spelling errors, such as Kannada ಹಬ್ನದ for ಹಬ್ಬದ and Marathi अणि for आणि.

faqs.question: How do you say Happy Diwali in Tamil?
faqs.answer: Say தீபாவளி நல்வாழ்த்துகள் (tīpāvaḷi nalvāḻttukaḷ), literally "Deepavali good blessings", or add இனிய ("sweet") in front. Tamil households greet on the morning of Naraka Chaturdashi, which Drik Panchang puts on Thursday 28 October 2027.

faqs.question: How do you say Happy Diwali in Kannada?
faqs.answer: ದೀಪಾವಳಿ ಹಬ್ಬದ ಶುಭಾಶಯಗಳು (dīpāvaḷi habbada śubhāśayagaḷu) means "auspicious wishes of the Deepavali festival". Check the doubled ಬ in ಹಬ್ಬದ; Kittel's dictionary lists ಹಬ್ಬ as "a festival".

faqs.question: What is Happy Diwali in Marathi?
faqs.answer: दिवाळीच्या हार्दिक शुभेच्छा (divāḷīcyā hārdik śubhecchā), "heartfelt good wishes of Diwali". Molesworth's 1857 dictionary treats Diwali as the days from Narakachaturdashi to Yamadvitiya, which fall from 28 to 31 October in 2027.

faqs.question: How do you say Happy Diwali in Sanskrit?
faqs.answer: One form is दीपोत्सवस्य शुभाशयाः (dīpotsavasya śubhāśayāḥ), "good wishes of the lamp festival". Apte's dictionary confirms each part, but the compound शुभाशयाः is modern usage rather than a dictionary headword.

faqs.question: What does Deepavali literally mean?
faqs.answer: "Row of lamps", from Sanskrit dīpa ("lamp") and āvali ("row"). Turner's comparative dictionary, entry 6358, shows how it became diwālī, divāḷī, deāli and diārī in different languages.

faqs.question: Should I say Diwali Mubarak or Saal Mubarak in Gujarati?
faqs.answer: They mean different things. સાલ મુબારક is "Happy New Year", said on the Gujarati new year, Saturday 30 October 2027; for Diwali itself Wiktionary's example is દિવાળીની શુભકામનાઓ, though દિવાળી મુબારક is also used.

faqs.question: What do people in Nepal call Diwali?
faqs.answer: Tihar (तिहार). A Nepali greeting is तिहारको शुभकामना (tihārko śubhakāmanā), "Tihar's good wishes", and Nepali spells the festival's other name दिपावली, with a short i.

faqs.question: Is it நல்வாழ்த்துகள் or நல்வாழ்த்துக்கள்?
faqs.answer: Both appear in print. Wiktionary gives வாழ்த்துகள் as the plural of வாழ்த்து, while its own example sentence uses the doubled-k form, so choose one and stay consistent.

faqs.question: Which greetings on this list could not be fully checked?
faqs.answer: Five points: the Sanskrit and Kannada compounds (both halves verified, not the whole), Assamese শুভেচ্ছা (checked only in Bengali sources), the grammatical endings in Punjabi, Odia and Assamese, and Konkani, which is left out.

faqs.question: Can I write a Tamil or Bengali wish inside SubhSandesh's Diwali card?
faqs.answer: Yes. The wishes, the diya tag and the letter are lines you write yourself, so any script goes in as typed; we have not tested every script in every field, so preview the page on a phone before sending the link.

faqs.question: Why does diwala mean bankrupt in Hindi?
faqs.answer: Turner's dictionary records that a failed merchant's house was marked with lamps, which gave Hindi diwālā, "bankruptcy". The Tamil Lexicon also lists a second தீபாவளி meaning "insolvent", so avoid puns on it.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Happy Diwali in Different Languages, Checked Word by Word

Happy Diwali in different languages reads दिवाली की शुभकामनाएँ (divālī kī śubhkāmnāẽ) in Hindi, தீபாவளி நல்வாழ்த்துகள் (tīpāvaḷi nalvāḻttukaḷ) in Tamil, ದೀಪಾವಳಿ ಹಬ್ಬದ ಶುಭಾಶಯಗಳು (dīpāvaḷi habbada śubhāśayagaḷu) in Kannada and दिवाळीच्या हार्दिक शुभेच्छा (divāḷīcyā hārdik śubhecchā) in Marathi. Nearly every version has three parts: the festival's name, a word meaning "of", and a noun for good wishes.

A typo is costly: 48.3% of pages shared on SubhSandesh are opened on a phone, and each page is viewed 11.1 times on average (measured 24 September 2026, all page types; no Diwali data exists yet), so a misspelt line is read again and again. Below are 14 languages with script, transliteration, literal meaning and the dictionary each word was checked against, plus the 2027 day each region says it.

## What does "Happy Diwali" mean in Indian languages?

An Indian-language Diwali greeting usually says "good wishes of Diwali", not "happy Diwali". Hindi शुभकामना, Marathi शुभेच्छा, Telugu శుభాకాంక్షలు and Kannada ಶುಭಾಶಯ all start with Sanskrit śubha, "auspicious", plus a word for wish.

The festival's name goes back to Sanskrit दीपावलि (dīpāvali), "row of lamps". Ralph Turner's [Comparative Dictionary of the Indo-Aryan Languages, entry 6358](https://dsal.uchicago.edu/cgi-bin/app/soas_query.py?qs=d%C4%ABp%C4%81vali&searchhws=yes&matchtype=exact) traces how speech wore it down: Hindi and Punjabi diwālī, Gujarati and Marathi divāḷī, Bengali deāli, Bhojpuri diārī, Sindhi ḍ̠iārī.

Deepavali is the other branch. Tamil, Kannada, Telugu, Malayalam and formal Bengali borrowed the Sanskrit word directly (per Wiktionary), so they keep the p that Hindi lost.

## Happy Diwali in 14 languages, with the source for each word

Each line was checked word by word on 22 October 2026, mostly against printed dictionaries scanned by the University of Chicago's Digital Dictionaries of South Asia (DSAL), and against Wiktionary where an old dictionary predates the word. "Literal" means a word-for-word gloss.

| Language | Greeting | Transliteration | Literal meaning | Checked against |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hindi | दिवाली की शुभकामनाएँ | divālī kī śubhkāmnāẽ | Diwali's good wishes | Wiktionary; Platts p. 531 |
| Urdu | دیوالی مبارک | dīwālī mubārak | Diwali, blessed | Platts pp. 560, 988 |
| Sanskrit | दीपोत्सवस्य शुभाशयाः | dīpotsavasya śubhāśayāḥ | good wishes of the lamp festival | Apte pp. 817, 1562, 367 |
| Marathi | दिवाळीच्या हार्दिक शुभेच्छा | divāḷīcyā hārdik śubhecchā | heartfelt good wishes of Diwali | Molesworth p. 414; Wiktionary |
| Gujarati | દિવાળીની શુભકામનાઓ | divāḷīnī śubhkāmnāo | good wishes of Diwali | Wiktionary |
| Punjabi | ਦਿਵਾਲੀ ਦੀਆਂ ਵਧਾਈਆਂ | divālī dīā̃ vadhāīā̃ | congratulations of Diwali | Wiktionary (Maya Singh 1895) |
| Bengali | শুভ দীপাবলি | śubhô dipabôli | auspicious Deepavali | Samsad p. 782; Wiktionary |
| Odia | ଦୀପାବଳିର ଶୁଭେଚ୍ଛା | dīpābaḷira śubhecchā | Deepavali's good wish | Purnachandra pp. 3788, 7754 |
| Assamese | দেৱালীৰ শুভেচ্ছা | dewālīr śubhecchā | Dewali's good wish | Wiktionary (name only) |
| Nepali | तिहारको शुभकामना | tihārko śubhakāmanā | Tihar's good wishes | Wiktionary |
| Tamil | தீபாவளி நல்வாழ்த்துகள் | tīpāvaḷi nalvāḻttukaḷ | Deepavali good blessings | Tamil Lexicon pp. 1942, 2169, 3620 |
| Telugu | దీపావళి శుభాకాంక్షలు | dīpāvaḷi śubhākāṅkṣalu | Deepavali auspicious wishes | Brown pp. 107, 1262; Wiktionary |
| Kannada | ದೀಪಾವಳಿ ಹಬ್ಬದ ಶುಭಾಶಯಗಳು | dīpāvaḷi habbada śubhāśayagaḷu | Deepavali festival's good wishes | Kittel pp. 838, 1707, 1537, 176 |
| Malayalam | ദീപാവലി ആശംസകൾ | dīpāvali āśaṁsakaḷ | Deepavali wishes | Gundert p. 94; Wiktionary |

Five things could not be fully verified. The compounds शुभाशयाः (Sanskrit) and ಶುಭಾಶಯ (Kannada) are not headwords in Apte or Kittel, though both halves are; Assamese শুভেচ্ছা was checked only in Bengali sources; the "of" endings in Punjabi, Odia and Assamese are grammar, not dictionary entries; and Konkani is missing because no Konkani dictionary we could open gave a Diwali greeting.

## Happy Diwali in Tamil, Kannada, Marathi and Sanskrit, word by word

All four are separate searches in India's Google autocomplete (22 October 2026). Each entry gives the words, the day, and the spelling trap we saw on live pages.

### Tamil: தீபாவளி நல்வாழ்த்துகள்

The words are தீபாவளி, then நல் (nal, "good", [Tamil Lexicon](https://dsal.uchicago.edu/cgi-bin/app/tamil-lex_query.py?qs=%E0%AE%A4%E0%AF%80%E0%AE%AA%E0%AE%BE%E0%AE%B5%E0%AE%B3%E0%AE%BF&searchhws=yes&matchtype=exact) p. 2169), then வாழ்த்து (vāḻttu, "benediction, felicitation", p. 3620) with the plural -கள். Put இனிய (iṉiya, "sweet, pleasant") in front for a warmer line.

The Lexicon (p. 1942) places Deepavali at dawn on the 14th day of dark Aippaci, with a ritual bath. Drik Panchang lists Tamil Deepavali on Thursday 28 October 2027; some Tamil Nadu holiday listings say Friday 29 October, so confirm with the family.

The trap is the plural. Wiktionary gives வாழ்த்துகள், yet its own example writes வாழ்த்துக்கள்; both appear in print, so pick one and keep it.

### Kannada: ದೀಪಾವಳಿ ಹಬ್ಬದ ಶುಭಾಶಯಗಳು

The words are ದೀಪಾವಳಿ, then ಹಬ್ಬ (habba, "a festival", Kittel p. 1707) with -ದ for "of", then ಶುಭ ("auspicious") joined to ಆಶಯ, whose fourth sense in Kittel is "wish or will", plus the plural -ಗಳು. [Kittel's entry for ದೀಪಾವಳಿ (revised edition, 1968–1971)](https://dsal.uchicago.edu/cgi-bin/app/kittel_query.py?qs=%E0%B2%A6%E0%B3%80%E0%B2%AA%E0%B2%BE%E0%B2%B5%E0%B2%B3%E0%B2%BF&searchhws=yes&matchtype=exact) describes a festival of lights honouring Bali on the first day of bright Kārttika. That is Bali Padyami, Saturday 30 October 2027 in Drik Panchang.

The trap is ಬ್ಬ. One of the five top-ranking pages in India on 22 October 2026 printed ಹಬ್ನದ, with ನ where the doubled ಬ belongs.

### Marathi: दिवाळीच्या हार्दिक शुभेच्छा

The words are दिवाळी, then -च्या ("of"), हार्दिक (hārdik, "heartfelt") and शुभेच्छा (śubhecchā, "good wish", from śubha plus icchā). [Molesworth's 1857 Marathi dictionary](https://dsal.uchicago.edu/cgi-bin/app/molesworth_query.py?qs=%E0%A4%A6%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B3%E0%A5%80&searchhws=yes&matchtype=exact) defines divāḷī as running from Narakachaturdashi to Yamadvitiya inclusive. In 2027 that is Thursday 28 to Sunday 31 October, so the line works on any of the four days.

The trap is the word for "and". Two top-five pages print अणि, but Molesworth (p. 67) spells it आणि.

### Sanskrit: दीपोत्सवस्य शुभाशयाः

The words are दीप (dīpa, "lamp") plus उत्सव (utsava, "festival") with -स्य for "of", then शुभ plus आशय, which Apte glosses as "intention" and "will or pleasure", in the plural. Apte's dictionary lists dīpotsava and dīpāvalī under दीप: "a row of lights" and "the festival called Diwali held on the night of new moon in Āśvina". With no regional day attached, it suits any date from 27 to 31 October 2027.

The trap is overconfidence. शुभाशयाः is modern usage assembled from verified parts, not a phrase Apte prints whole.

## Tihar, Diyari, Dewali: the festival's other names

Nepali speakers call the festival तिहार (tihār), and Wiktionary gives दिपावली (dipāwalī, short i) as its synonym. Assamese inherited দেৱালী (dewali), with দীপাৱলি as the learned twin, and Turner's entry adds Awadhi dewārī and Kashmiri zuwū̆lᵘ, "festal arrangement of lamps".

Two more meanings sit in the same dictionaries. Turner's addenda record Kutchi ḍīyārī as "last day of the year (30th Aśvin)", which matches the Gujarati new year the next morning, when the greeting becomes સાલ મુબારક (sāl mubārak), "Happy New Year".

The other is money. Turner notes that a failed merchant's house was marked with lamps, which gave Hindi diwālā, "bankruptcy", and the Tamil Lexicon lists a second தீபாவளி meaning "insolvent".

## Which day each language says Happy Diwali in 2027

Diwali 2027 runs from Wednesday 27 to Sunday 31 October. The day each language calls "Diwali" differs, as its own dictionary shows.

| Day in 2027 | Who greets | Greeting | Dictionary basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| Thu 28 Oct, dawn | Tamil households | தீபாவளி நல்வாழ்த்துகள் | Tamil Lexicon: 14th of dark Aippaci, at dawn |
| Fri 29 Oct, evening | Hindi, Urdu, Punjabi, Odia, Bengali | दिवाली की शुभकामनाएँ | Platts: new moon of Kārttik; Purnachandra: Kārttika amāvāsyā |
| Sat 30 Oct | Gujarati, Kannada | સાલ મુબારક; ದೀಪಾವಳಿ ಹಬ್ಬದ ಶುಭಾಶಯಗಳು | Wiktionary: "Happy New Year"; Kittel: Bali's day |
| Thu 28 to Sun 31 Oct | Marathi | दिवाळीच्या हार्दिक शुभेच्छा | Molesworth: Narakachaturdashi to Yamadvitiya |

So a Tamil greeting sent on Friday evening arrives a day late. Drik Panchang also lists Bengal's Kali Puja on Thursday 28 October, and Sikh and Jain families keep these nights for their own reasons.

## How to check a greeting in a language you cannot read

Split the line into words and look each one up on DSAL. A word that returns nothing deserves a second opinion from a speaker.

Expect several Roman spellings, none of them "correct". The [Aksharantar paper (Findings of EMNLP 2023)](https://aclanthology.org/2023.findings-emnlp.4/) says transliteration matters in India because of multiple scripts and widespread romanized input; its dataset holds 26 million word pairs across 21 languages and 12 scripts. Send the native script, with the Roman line as a reading aid.

Do not judge the language by its script. The [Unicode Consortium's Indic FAQ](https://www.unicode.org/faq/indic.html) counts nine major Brahmi-derived scripts of India and says scripts and languages do not map one-to-one: Hindi, Marathi, Nepali and Sanskrit share Devanagari, and Assamese writes ৰ and ৱ in a Bengali-type script. One top-five page printed its "Assamese" line in Devanagari.

If the greeting is for one person, SubhSandesh's [interactive Diwali card with a diya at their door](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-diwali) puts it on the diya's tag, on a row of wish diyas and in a letter sealed in a red-and-gold liffafa. Every line is editable, so a Tamil or Odia sentence goes in as typed; we have not tested every script in every field, so preview on a phone. It takes about five minutes, and the private link opens in any browser with no app.

Mind the timing. On Raksha Bandhan 2026, our nearest festival data (n = 89 pages), 49.4% of pages were built on the day itself, too late for a Tamil greeting meant for dawn on 28 October. For a friend from another state spending this Diwali away from you, our [miss-you page](https://subhsandesh.in/missyou-gf) fits better than festival scenes.

## When a translated greeting is the wrong choice

Skip the translation if you cannot check it and the recipient is a native speaker you are close to. A careful line in your own language beats a broken one in theirs.

SubhSandesh is also the wrong tool in three cases: a society group of dozens, an elder without a smartphone, and anyone you will greet in person on 29 October 2027. Say it aloud then, and send nothing.

## Sources

- Turner, *A Comparative Dictionary of the Indo-Aryan Languages*, entry 6358, 1962–1966, supplements 1969–1985 — [DSAL](https://dsal.uchicago.edu/cgi-bin/app/soas_query.py?qs=d%C4%ABp%C4%81vali&searchhws=yes&matchtype=exact).
- *Tamil Lexicon*, University of Madras, 1924–1936 — [DSAL](https://dsal.uchicago.edu/cgi-bin/app/tamil-lex_query.py?qs=%E0%AE%A4%E0%AF%80%E0%AE%AA%E0%AE%BE%E0%AE%B5%E0%AE%B3%E0%AE%BF&searchhws=yes&matchtype=exact).
- Kittel, *Kittel's Kannada-English Dictionary*, revised edition, University of Madras, 1968–1971 — [DSAL](https://dsal.uchicago.edu/cgi-bin/app/kittel_query.py?qs=%E0%B2%A6%E0%B3%80%E0%B2%AA%E0%B2%BE%E0%B2%B5%E0%B2%B3%E0%B2%BF&searchhws=yes&matchtype=exact).
- Molesworth, *A Dictionary, Marathi and English*, 1857 — [DSAL](https://dsal.uchicago.edu/cgi-bin/app/molesworth_query.py?qs=%E0%A4%A6%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B3%E0%A5%80&searchhws=yes&matchtype=exact).
- Madhani et al., "Aksharantar", Findings of EMNLP, December 2023, abstract read — [ACL Anthology](https://aclanthology.org/2023.findings-emnlp.4/).
- Unicode Consortium, "Indic Scripts and Languages" FAQ, undated — [unicode.org](https://www.unicode.org/faq/indic.html).
- Also consulted: Platts (1884), Apte, Brown (1903), Gundert, Samsad, Purnachandra, Wiktionary; Drik Panchang for 2027 dates.

Kittel's Kannada-English Dictionary (rev. ed., University of Madras, 1968–1971), ದೀಪಾವಳಿ p. 838: 'a row of lamps or lights; a festival with nocturnal illuminations in honor of Balicakravarti in the śuddha pāḍya of the month of kārttika'. Also verified: ಹಬ್ಬ 'a festival' p. 1707; ಶುಭ 'auspicious' p. 1537; ಆಶಯ sense 4 'wish or will' p. 176. Reference instrument (cap-exempt).
Molesworth, A Dictionary, Marathi and English (2nd ed., 1857), दिवाळी p. 414: festival 'from नरकचतुर्दशी to यमद्वितीया inclusive'; आणि 'And' p. 67. Reference instrument (cap-exempt).

Madhani et al., 'Aksharantar', Findings of EMNLP 2023 (peer-reviewed, open access): 'Transliteration is very important in the Indian language context due to the usage of multiple scripts and the widespread use of romanized inputs'; dataset of 26 million transliteration pairs for 21 Indic languages from 3 language families using 12 scripts. Abstract read; full PDF not read.

Unicode Consortium, Indic Scripts and Languages FAQ: Indic scripts in the narrow sense are the nine major Brahmi-derived scripts of India; 'There is not a one-to-one relation between Indic scripts and languages… many languages are written in multiple scripts.' Undated page; standards body (cap-exempt).
